key_insight: ConGLUDe is a single contrastive geometric model that unifies structure‑ and ligand‑based drug design by learning joint protein and ligand embeddings, enabling end‑to‑end tasks (binding prediction, ligand retrieval/generation) from one shared representation.
problem_solved: Removes the separation between structure‑based and ligand‑based pipelines—addressing incompatible data sources and modeling assumptions—so models can be trained jointly at scale and transfer knowledge across drug‑design tasks.
method: Geometric protein encoder that produces whole‑protein representations and implicit embeddings of predicted binding regions (avoids needing explicit pocket labels).
Contrastive learning objective aligns protein and ligand embeddings in a shared latent space using positive (binders) and negative (decoy) pairs.
Unified training enables downstream uses (affinity scoring, ligand retrieval/generation, docking‑aware scoring) from one model without separate pipelines.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners a scalable, single representation and training paradigm that reduces engineering complexity, improves transfer across tasks, and increases sample efficiency for computational drug discovery.

paper_title: Contrastive Geometric Learning Unlocks Unified Structure- and Ligand-Based Drug Design
paper_authors: Lisa Schneckenreiter, Sohvi Luukkonen, Lukas Friedrich, Daniel Kuhn, Günter Klambauer
